# Binding manifest

Every key `spec/binding-schema.json` allows in a `binding.yaml`, block by block, with the keys it shares with a process adapter's `manifest.json` (`spec/schemas/manifest.schema.json`). A dotted key sits inside the key before the dot, and an upper-case part such as `FIELD` stands for a name you choose.

A tier-1 adapter: a YAML document the runner's generic HTTP engine interprets deterministically (SPEC.md §10a, ADR-022). Validate after decoding the YAML to JSON. Deliberately ~8 primitives; the moment a binding needs logic it graduates to a process adapter — no expression language may ever grow in here. Templating (ADR-057, M31): a leaf is a Liquid object in gtme's one bounded dialect over 'record.\<field\>', 'config.\<key\>', 'variables.\<name\>' and 'session' — objects only, no block tags, the fixed filter allowlist (SPEC.md §10 item 10; 'default' is the fallback: '{{ record.linkedin_url | default: record.linkedin_internal_url }}'). A leaf that is exactly one placeholder substitutes the typed value; leaves resolving to empty/null are omitted from the request (omitempty). The retired '{{a|b}}' alternatives fail verify naming the rewrite. In a deliver body, an object may carry the key '$variables': true — the resolved variables: mapping (minus any variable referenced individually elsewhere in the body) is spliced into that object. The engine pre-fills config defaults declared in config_schema.

## Manifest surface

The keys that say what the binding is. `Process manifest` says whether a process adapter's manifest has the same key; where the binding schema gives no description, the process manifest's is shown.

| Key | Type | Required | Description | Process manifest |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | yes | Adapter id, such as 'attio/assert'. Named by the contract owner (ADR-026). The id's vendor prefix is the COST provider name. | same key |
| `version` | integer | yes | Process manifest: Manifest version; part of the provenance string. | same key |
| `role` | one of `source`, `traverse`, `enrich`, `deliver` | yes | source: pagination + cursor/STATE, config 'limit' caps emitted records; traverse (ADR-054): a source-shaped request templated per parent from '{{record.\<field\>}}' placeholders (its needs), emitting records of entity_type related to the parent by 'relation', 'limit' capping children per parent; enrich: per-record request; deliver: idempotency + dry-run receipts. | same key |
| `entity_type` | string | yes | A type file's name (SPEC.md §4a). For a traverse this is the OUTPUT type; 'from' is the input. A binding MAY ship the type it emits as types/\<name\>.json beside binding.yaml (never an embedded name). | same key |
| `from` | string | no | Traverse only (ADR-054): the input type; the planner requires it to equal the current segment's type. | same key |
| `relation` | object | no | Traverse only (ADR-054): the edge written between every emitted record and its parent, and which end it starts at (record: authored_by from the post to its author; parent: works_at from the person to the company). | same key |
| `relation.name` | string matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` | yes | — | same key |
| `relation.from` | one of `record`, `parent` | yes | — | same key |
| `needs` | any | no | Same manifest surface as process adapters (SPEC.md §6): a JSON Schema, 'dynamic', or the dynamic-with-floor object form. | same key |
| `provides` | any | no | Same manifest surface as process adapters (SPEC.md §6). | same key |
| `config_schema` | object | no | Process manifest: JSON Schema for the step's `with:` block. | same key |
| `freshness_days` | integer | no | Process manifest: Default cache window for the fields this adapter provides; overridable per step with `cache:` (SPEC.md §6, §9). | same key |
| `cost_estimate_usd` | number | no | Process manifest: Static per-record cost estimate. `gtme plan` prints '?' when absent (SPEC.md §7). | same key |
| `keep_payloads` | boolean | no | ADR-030: whether the engine attaches raw responses to this binding's RECORDs for retention. Default true; steps may override with keep_payloads: false in config. | same key |
| `payload_ttl_days` | integer | no | ADR-030: retention window for this binding's payloads (default 90). 0 = no expiry. | same key |
| `credentials` | array of string | no | Process manifest: Env var names the runner MUST inject. A missing one is a plan-time error (SPEC.md §6). | same key |
| `credentials_optional` | array of string | no | Process manifest: Injected when present, never blocks a plan (SPEC.md §6). Used by adapters that can work several ways, such as an AI step with a local engine. | same key |
| `idempotency` | one of `native`, `ledger` | no | Which party guarantees delivery dedupe: the vendor's own semantics (native, such as an assert/upsert endpoint) or the runner's deliveries table (ledger). Required for role: deliver. | same key |
| `idempotency_scope` | string | no | Deliver bindings (ADR-044): config key whose resolved value scopes deliveries rows (SPEC §8). Optional. The key MUST hold a stable identifier of the destination (an id, an API slug, a file path, a URL), never a display name its owner can change (ADR-062); where the identifier has a shape, constrain the key to it in config_schema so a name is a plan error. | same key |

## Process manifest keys a binding does not take

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `emits_key_fields` | array of string | Sources only: which output fields the runner should build the identity key from (SPEC.md §6). |
| `batch` | boolean | Marks adapters the runner must feed in batches — the AI steps — one invocation per batch_size records (SPEC.md §6, §9). |
| `attests` | boolean | ADR-036, deliver adapters only: after a successful create the adapter re-reads the target and emits an ATTEST per record (SPEC.md §5) — confirmed \| contradicted \| inconclusive. Absent, every delivery stays `accepted` and is reported inconclusive (the honest default). |
| `preflights` | boolean | ADR-040, deliver adapters only: the adapter can check the live target against what a step is about to send (SPEC.md §5 PREFLIGHT) — read-only, at --dry-run and arm time. Absent, no preflight runs. |

## Auth

The `auth` block, optional.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auth.type` | one of `header`, `query`, `basic`, `bearer` | yes | — |
| `auth.name` | string | no | Header or query-param name; unused for basic/bearer. |
| `auth.env` | string | yes | Env var holding the credential (resolved per SPEC.md §6 credentials rules). |
| `auth.prefix` | string | no | Optional literal prefix for the value, such as 'Bearer '. |

## Request

The `request` block, required. Templating draws only from step config, the record's canonical fields, resolved variables, and the session id — no expressions, no computation.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `request.method` | one of `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` | yes | — |
| `request.url` | string | yes | — |
| `request.query` | map of string | no | Query-param templates; empty resolutions are omitted. |
| `request.headers` | map of string | no | — |
| `request.body` | any | no | Body template: a JSON shape whose string leaves are templates. Empty resolutions are omitted. '$variables': true in an object splices the resolved variables map. |

## Pagination

The `pagination` block, optional.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pagination.strategy` | one of `page`, `cursor`, `offset` | yes | — |
| `pagination.param` | string | no | Request param carrying the page number / cursor / offset. |
| `pagination.in` | one of `query`, `body` | no | Where pagination params ride (default query). |
| `pagination.cursor_path` | string | no | Dotted path to the next cursor in the response (cursor strategy). |
| `pagination.page_size` | integer or string | no | Records per page: an integer or a template (such as '{{config.per_page}}'). |
| `pagination.size_param` | string | no | Request param carrying the page size. |
| `pagination.termination` | object | no | — |
| `pagination.termination.empty_records` | boolean | no | Stop when a page yields zero records (engine default: always on). |
| `pagination.termination.short_page` | boolean | no | Stop when a page yields fewer records than page_size. |
| `pagination.termination.total_pages_path` | string | no | Dotted path to a total-page count; alternatives via '\|'. |
| `pagination.max` | integer | no | Hard cap on pages fetched. |

## Extract

The `extract` block, optional.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `extract.records` | string or array of string | yes | Dotted path to the record array (or single record) in the response; a list means first non-empty wins. |
| `extract.fields` | object | yes | canonical (or vendor-namespaced) field name -\> extraction rule. |
| `extract.fields.FIELD` | string or object | no | — |
| `extract.fields.FIELD.path` | string | no | — |
| `extract.fields.FIELD.paths` | array of string | no | Alternatives; first non-empty wins. |
| `extract.fields.FIELD.transform` | string | no | A registry normalization rule id (SPEC.md §4a) — or 'linkedin', the engine-owned §4 classify-and-route rule that stores a LinkedIn-URL-shaped value under the field matching its shape. Never arbitrary logic. |
| `extract.fields.FIELD.absent` | array of any | no | Sentinel values the vendor uses to mean 'no value' (such as a locked-email placeholder, or 0 for an unknown count); matched exactly, treated as absent. |
| `extract.fields.FIELD.skip_if_input` | boolean | no | Omit this output field when the projected input already carried a non-empty value for it (for example, only emit a resolved public linkedin_url when the record arrived without one). |
| `extract.fields.FIELD.each` | string | no | The list form (SPEC.md §10a, ADR-059): a dotted path to an array ('\|' alternatives allowed, first non-empty wins). The template renders once per element over item.*, a render that is empty after trimming is dropped, rendering stops at limit, and the field provides an array of strings. Does not mix with path, paths or transform. |
| `extract.fields.FIELD.template` | string | no | The each: template, in the ADR-057 dialect over item.* — tags allowed, since it renders text, not a typed value. Only with each. |
| `extract.fields.FIELD.limit` | integer or string | no | The most renders each: keeps: a positive integer, or a config reference ({{ config.\<key\> }}). Only with each; omitted means every element. |

## Errors

The `errors` block, optional. HTTP status (or status class like '4xx') -\> verdict mapping; statuses the map does not name follow the engine's default classification (SPEC.md §8 exit-code classes).

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `errors.STATUS` | object | no | — |
| `errors.STATUS.verdict` | one of `fail_record`, `fail_run`, `retry`, `skip` | yes | — |
| `errors.STATUS.reason` | string | no | — |

## Cost

The `cost` block, optional.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cost.per` | one of `record`, `request`, `unit` | no | — |
| `cost.amount_usd` | number or string matching `^\s*\{\{[^{}]+\}\}\s*$` | no | Dollars per unit of `per`: a number, or a template resolved from config (such as '{{config.cost_per_record_usd}}') for vendors whose price is plan-dependent (ADR-046). Declare the knob in config_schema. An unresolved template costs $0 at run time and `gtme plan` prints `est/record: unset`. A page-billed endpoint declares `per: request` — `per: record` counts emitted records, and a `limit` truncates emission after the vendor has billed the page. |
| `cost.unit_path` | string | no | Dotted path to a units-consumed count in the response (per: unit). |

## Retry

The `retry` block, optional.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `retry.max_attempts` | integer | no | — |
| `retry.backoff_seconds` | number | no | — |
| `retry.rate_per_hour` | integer | no | — |
| `retry.windows` | array of string | no | Hourly send/fetch windows, such as '09:00-17:00'. |

## Session

The `session` block, optional. Optional pagination-consistency session: a UUID minted per run and passed through on every request.

| Key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `session.param` | string | no | — |
| `session.in` | one of `header`, `query`, `body` | no | — |

## Example

From `spec/bindings/apollo-search/binding.yaml`:

```yaml
# apollo/search — THE apollo/search adapter (built into gtme until ADR-059),
# rewritten for the masked API surface (ADR-043). Apollo withdrew value
# fields from API search 2026-08-30: `mixed_people/search` 422s for API
# callers, and its replacement `mixed_people/api_search` returns masked rows
# (no email, no linkedin, `has_*` booleans, obfuscated last name). This
# binding is honest about that: it provides the masked surface at $0, and
# the revealed person is apollo/enrich's job — the canonical composition
# filters on these free fields first and reveals only past the filter.
#
# Identity (§4): a masked row carries no email, no linkedin and no company
# domain, so identity derives from the name-hash tier — which needs a first
# AND last name. `last_name` therefore carries Apollo's own obfuscated form
# (e.g. "D.") rather than being dropped: it keys the record, `gtme plan`
# notes the weak tier, and apollo/enrich supersedes it with the real value
# on reveal. Distinct people who share a first name and an obfuscated
# initial in one pull would collide on this tier — reveal early if that
# matters.
#
# Endpoint: POST https://api.apollo.io/api/v1/mixed_people/api_search
# Auth:     X-Api-Key header
# Docs:     https://docs.apollo.io/reference/people-api-search

id: apollo/search
version: 2
role: source
entity_type: person

provides:
  type: object
  additionalProperties: false
  properties:
    first_name: { type: string }
    last_name: { type: string }
    title: { type: string }
    company_name: { type: string }
    apollo.id: { type: string }
    apollo.has_email: { type: boolean }

config_schema:
  type: object
  additionalProperties: false
  anyOf:
    - required: [query]
    - required: [titles]
    - required: [seniorities]
    - required: [locations]
    - required: [domains]
  properties:
    query:
      type: string
      description: Free-text search, such as "vp marketing, saas, 50-200 employees"
    limit:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
      description: Stop after this many people
    titles:
      type: array
      items: { type: string }
      description: person_titles
    seniorities:
      type: array
      items: { type: string }
      description: person_seniorities
    locations:
      type: array
      items: { type: string }
      description: organization_locations
    employee_ranges:
      type: array
      items: { type: string }
      description: organization_num_employees_ranges, such as "50,200"
    domains:
      type: array
      items: { type: string }
      description: q_organization_domains
    per_page:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 100
      default: 25
    base_url:
      type: string
      default: "https://api.apollo.io"
      description: Override the API host (testing)

credentials: [APOLLO_API_KEY]
cost_estimate_usd: 0

auth:
  type: header
  name: X-Api-Key
  env: APOLLO_API_KEY

request:
  method: POST
  url: "{{config.base_url}}/api/v1/mixed_people/api_search"
  headers:
    Cache-Control: no-cache
  body:
    q_keywords: "{{config.query}}"
    person_titles: "{{config.titles}}"
    person_seniorities: "{{config.seniorities}}"
    organization_locations: "{{config.locations}}"
    organization_num_employees_ranges: "{{config.employee_ranges}}"
    q_organization_domains_list: "{{config.domains}}"

pagination:
  strategy: page
  param: page
  in: body
  size_param: per_page
  page_size: "{{config.per_page}}"
  termination:
    empty_records: true
    short_page: true

extract:
  records: people
  fields:
    apollo.id: id
    first_name: first_name
    last_name: last_name_obfuscated
    title: title
    company_name: organization.name
    apollo.has_email: has_email

cost:
  per: record
  amount_usd: 0
```
